title: Your Smart Classroom Management Report Card nt-report-card/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: As the school year ends, Linsin offers teachers a self-evaluation tool built around fifteen core SCM principles, urging them to grade themselves honestly from A to F on each before summer distractions take over. The fifteen items cover the full range of SCM's philosophy, including consistently following a classroom management plan, enforcing consequences calmly like a referee, avoiding intimidation, building rapport through kindness, praising only for genuine accomplishment, favoring intrinsic over external motivation, and maintaining low personal stress while enjoying teaching. He frames the exercise as a private, judgment-free opportunity for insight that a teacher might not otherwise arrive at, and points readers to the site's archive, books, and guides for follow-up on any item that raises questions. Linsin closes with a personal note wishing readers a good summer and inviting topic suggestions for future articles.
points: A self-graded report card built from fifteen core SCM principles helps teachers honestly assess their year before summer break.
Items span consistency, calm enforcement, kindness-based rapport, intrinsic motivation, and personal well-being and stress management.
Brutal honesty in self-grading is presented as the key to becoming a happier, more effective teacher the following year.
The report card is offered as a downloadable PDF meant to be completed immediately, before summer distractions set in.
Every item on the report card connects back to material already covered extensively on the SCM website, books, and guides.
quotes: Before you peel out of the parking lot and into the summer sun—or even if you have already—and while it’s still fresh in your mind, it’s smart to do a quick self-evaluation.
Give yourself a grade of A through F for each item to the degree they were accomplished.
Just be sure to be brutally honest with yourself. It’s key to becoming a happier, more effective teacher next year.
I taught routines thoroughly and held my class accountable for performing them with excellence.
I prepared efficiently and had ample time to spend with my family and the hobbies I enjoy.
A self-evaluation when no one is watching can be a powerful experience, allowing you to gain insights that otherwise may not occur to you.
